review.reason: Both describe Coruscant Ventures' "SAO Many SAOs" / "SaO MANY SAOs" board (same GitHub repo DC33-SaO-MANY-SAOs, 25 SAO slots, dual-18650 power, companion SmartAO LED module, DC33/2025), just documented via different storefronts (maker's own site vs. Hacker Warehouse). Both entries claim to be "the official DEF CON 29 human badge," same maker (MK Factor/Whiteleys), same event/year, and both explicitly disclaim being the other well-known DC29 community badges (AND!XOR, Whiskey Pirates) — so they're intended to describe the same physical object, not different items. However, the two entries give contradictory hardware/functionality: dc29-badge (MCU ATSAMD21G16B, 4-key mechanical macropad, CR2032, Discord mic/emote control, sourced from Hackaday) vs dc29-badge-2021 (MCU MC56F8006VLC, RGB keys + touch sensors, rechargeable USB battery, networked Simon Says/CTF game, sourced from Science Viking Labs). This is too large a factual conflict to be a mere colorway/second-run variant, but both plausibly reference the actual single official DC29 badge with one entry's research being wrong/conflated with a different con's badge — so I can't confidently rule out these being two genuinely different physical badges. Recommend a human check the primary sources (Hackaday vs Science Viking Labs) before merging; if merged, dc29-badge-2021 has higher stated research confidence and a more detailed, internally consistent functional description.
